title: Shuttleboard — Release ops scratchlist
content:
Quick notes for tonight's Shuttle release (staging -> prod). This is my personal scratchlist — informal, chronological, and intentionally terse. Use channel #release-ops for comms; ping me directly for lift.

Pre-cutover (T minus 90 to 15m)
- T-90m: Final smoke on staging (run smoke.sh on staging cluster). Expected: all health checks green, 0 5xx in last 5m.
- T-75m: Ensure canary config evaluated: /configs/canary-v2 loaded in console and rollout=0.05.
- T-60m: Run backport checklist (below). Note any merge conflicts here.
- T-45m: Scale read replicas down to 2 before migration window (k8s: scale deployment cache-reader --replicas=2 -n prod).
- T-30m: Preflight scripts: ./ops/preflight/verify_network.sh, ./ops/preflight/check_ssh_keys.sh
- T-20m: Postgres read replica catchup check (psql show replication status). Expect lag < 2s.
- T-10m: Announce in #release-ops: "Shuttle release starting in 10m — no hotfix merges unless labeled emergency." Use template (see Comms section).
- T-5m: Grab a snapshot of all prod ASGs and instance counts. Save to /tmp/shuttle-asg-snapshot-<ts>.log

Backport and PRs (handy copy)
- REL-4821: backport hotfix for kv-cache eviction race
  - PR: serving-runtime#1297 -> cherry-pick onto release-2026-03. Run unit tests locally (pytest -q tests/eviction_test.py)
  - Status: merged to release branch at 2026-03-10 21:08 by Marta
- REL-4833: config validator fix
  - PR: infra-config#482 -> needs backport, conflicts in config-schema.yaml
  - Action: open backport PR from branch rel/4833-backport, assign Ethan, add label 'backport:manual'

Commands I keep typing (save locally):
- kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/serving-runtime --watch
- gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels=release:shuttle" --format=json > /tmp/shuttle-instances.json
- ./ops/deploy.sh --env prod --image gcr.io/redwood/serving-runtime:shuttle-20260310
- ./ops/monitoring/check_token_usage.sh --window 5m

Cutover runbook (rough sequence)
1) Lock merges: set GitHub branch protection to require all checks (done by GitHub UI quick toggle)
2) Disable auto-scaling for serving-runtime node-pool (reason: avoid churn during migration)
3) Apply DB schema change (if needed) behind feature flag (DB script: sql/migrations/20260310_add_kv_index.sql)
   - If migration fails: revert via backup sql/backups/pre-shuttle-20260310.sql
4) Deploy canary: deploy image tag shuttle-canary -> rollout 5% traffic to canary
5) Wait 5–10m; run smoke and perf checks. Look for increased tail latency or 5xx.
6) Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% (use console auto-rollout or ops/deploy ramp flag)
7) Post-deploy: verify tracing for top 10 routes (open jaeger and search trace ids emitted in logs)

Verification checklist (post each step):
- Health checks: /health returns 200 OK across all pods
- Error budget: SLO dashboard (console) shows errors < 0.5% in last 10m
- Latency: p99 should not increase > 20% vs baseline (baseline located in /dashboards/baselines/shuttle.json)
- Token consumption: embeddings/sec and generation tokens tracked; ensure no spike > 2x usual
- Logs: no repeated exceptions re: KV cache or OOMs in last 10m

Monitoring & dashboards to watch
- console > models > serving-runtime > latency-by-route
- Grafana: prod-inference/serving-runtime-main
- Sentry: production errors filtered by env:prod and release:shuttle-20260310
- Pager duty: be on-call list (Tom, Aisha, Jordan) for 90m post-full-deploy

Rollback plan (fast)
- If p99 > 2x baseline AND error rate > 1% for 10m -> immediate rollback to previous image tag
  - kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/serving-runtime --to-revision=<prev-rev>
  - Re-enable autoscaling if we had disabled it
  - Post-mortem: create REL-XXXX ticket with timestamps, attach logs + /tmp/asg snapshot

Comms snippets (copy these into slack)
- Pre-start (T-10m): "Heads up: Shuttle release starting in 10m. Expect brief traffic ramp. Please avoid non-emergency merges. @channel"
- Go/no-go check (T-1m): "Go-check: DB migration ok? (Marta), Canary deploy smoke green? (Ethan), Monitoring URLs up? (Jordan)" — wait for explicit ack
- Post-success: "Shuttle release complete — 100% traffic. Monitoring green. Team can resume normal merges in 30m. Thanks!"
- Rollback notice: "Rolling back Shuttle release due to elevated errors. Rolling back to img <prev-tag>. Follow-up RM to create incident ticket."

Notes to self / gotchas
- If k8s scheduling spikes with new image, drain one node and watch pod reschedules (kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets)
- Watch for TLS cert rotation job scheduled at 02:30 — could coincide with our window (check cronjobs in prod)
- Disk pressure on cache nodes: older images had a cleanup job disabled; make sure cleanup runs after deploy
- Remember to re-enable autoscaling after full ramp. I tend to forget.

Open questions / followups
- Should we bump the circuit breaker threshold on /generate for 10m to avoid cascading failures? (Pros: protects GPU pool; Cons: could increase latency)
- Need a small playbook for partial rollbacks by region (ap-southeast vs us-west) — follow up with infra on routing policy.

Post-release tasks (T+15m to T+90m)
- T+15m: Snapshot monitoring graphs + attach to REL-4821 ticket
- T+30m: Re-enable auto-scaling and remove release labels from instances
- T+60m: Draft short post-mortem note with findings (if anything abnormal)
- Close loop with CS for any customer impact messages

End of scratchlist — this is a live, personal note. Convert to a formal runbook if we repeat this pattern.
